title: Steering idler arm recall
ask: Has the 1985 steering idler-arm recall (NHTSA 85V108000) been done on your car, or is its idler arm sound today?
why: In 1985 Mazda recalled 1981-83 RX-7s (NHTSA 85V108000): the steering idler arm's pin corrodes once its dust seal fails, can seize, and can break - and then the steering is lost. The fix was a corrosion-resistant pin. Nothing in the record says whether your car had it, and after 40 years the original arm may have been replaced anyway. One 1982 owner who lost steering at 40 mph was told his VIN was not in the recall, so the VIN alone does not settle it. The idler arm sits on the frame rail on the passenger side, holding the far end of the centre link that the steering box pushes. Your answer decides whether the Manual lists it as a known fault to fix, or as checked.
options:
(a) Check it yourself: front wheels on the ground, have someone rock the steering wheel while you watch and hold the idler arm; any knock, visible play, a torn dust boot or a rusted pin means it is due. About 20 minutes, no parts.
(b) Replace the idler arm now without checking: a cheap aftermarket part and about an hour with a pickle fork; a parts round would pick it.
(c) Phone a Mazda dealer with the VIN and ask if 85V108000 was done: free, but records this old are often gone.
(d) It is already done or the arm is new: say when, if you know.
recommend: (a), unless you already know the arm has been replaced - then (d).
stops: Nothing in the projects. It is a safety check on the car as it is driven today; the Manual shows it as an open question until you answer.
